title: Relax pure bcc Fe bulk supercell
action: Perform spin-polarized DFT relaxation of a bulk bcc Fe supercell (e.g., 250-atom cell) using PBE-GGA and the chosen pseudopotentials. Converge with respect to plane-wave cutoff and k-point sampling. Record the total energy E_bulk and verify the equilibrium lattice parameter and magnetic moment.
description: Provides the reference bulk energy E_bulk used in the interaction energy formula.

title: Relax screw dislocation dipole in pure Fe
action: Construct a quadrupolar periodic array of 1/2⟨111⟩ screw dislocation dipoles in bcc Fe. Use two cell lengths along the dislocation line: 1b (135 Fe atoms) and 2b (270 Fe atoms). Relax atomic positions (fixed cell) with DFT using the same pseudopotentials/functional as the bulk step. Record the total energy E_easy for each cell length and save the relaxed easy‑core structure for later use.
description: Establishes the reference easy‑core dislocation energy, which enters the interaction energy definition, and provides the relaxed dislocation dipole template.

title: Relax isolated solutes in bulk Fe octahedral sites
action: For each solute X = B, C, N, O, place one solute atom in the octahedral interstitial site of a bulk Fe supercell (same cell size and DFT settings as step 01). Relax atomic positions and record the total energy E_X for each solute.
description: Yields the reference solute energies E_X required for computing the interaction energy.

title: DFT simulations of dislocation‑solute systems
action: For every combination of solute (B, C, N, O) and solute‑solute separation d = 1b, 2b: (a) construct the initial E₁ configuration by placing two solute atoms in octahedral‑like interstitial positions that are first nearest neighbours to each dislocation core, using the previously relaxed easy‑core dipole cell of the appropriate length; (b) fully relax the system with DFT; (c) determine from the relaxed structure whether the dislocation core has spontaneously reconstructed to the hard core with the solutes at the centre of regular trigonal prisms; (d) record the total energy E_dislo+X. For Fe(N) with d=1b, additionally construct the explicit hard‑core configuration (solutes directly at prismatic sites), relax it, and compare its energy with the spontaneous‑relaxation result to confirm that the reconstruction is energetically favourable even when not spontaneous. Store all raw energies and reconstruction flags in a structured intermediate file (raw_simulation_data.json).
description: Produces the total energies and reconstruction observations that are the basis for the scored interaction energies and reconstruction outcomes.

title: Compute interaction energies and write CSV
action: From the reference energies (E_bulk, E_easy for each cell length, E_X) and the dislocation‑solute energies recorded in raw_simulation_data.json, compute the dislocation–solute interaction energy per solute atom using E_int = E_d – E_∞ with E_d = ½ E_dislo+X + E_bulk and E_∞ = ½ E_easy + E_X. For each case, assign the reconstruction outcome: 'yes' if the dislocation core spontaneously transformed to the hard core, 'no' if not, or 'energetically_favorable_but_not_spontaneous' for the Fe(N)/1b exception. Write the results to interaction_energies.csv.
description: CSV file containing the solute‑dislocation interaction energy and reconstruction flag for all 8 main cases.
output_schema: Columns: solute (B|C|N|O), separation (1b|2b), E_int (float, eV), reconstruction_spontaneous (string: yes|no|energetically_favorable_but_not_spontaneous). Eight rows total.

title: Compile reconstruction summary JSON
action: From the same underlying data used for step 05a, produce a JSON file that summarises the reconstruction outcome and interaction energy for every solute–separation combination in a structured format.
description: JSON file mirroring the final interaction energies and reconstruction results.
